hints: Compare the proton numbers in each pair first, because the proton number decides which element an atom is.
Recall that isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers, so look for equal protons with $34$ versus $36$ or similar neutron difference.
Ignore a difference in electron number here because the question states some atoms are ionised, and losing or gaining electrons does not change the element or isotope.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Note that the number of electrons can differ because ionisation adds or removes electrons without changing proton or neutron numbers.
Check option A: protons $17$ and $19$ are different, so different elements.
Check option B: protons $23$ and $24$ are different, so different elements.

Check option C: protons are $29$ and $29$, so same element, while neutrons are $34$ and $36$, so different nucleon numbers. Electrons $29$ and $28$ show the second particle is a $+1$ ion, which does not affect isotope status.
Check option D: protons $32$ and $31$ are different, so different elements.
Therefore only the pair with equal protons and unequal neutrons qualifies. This is option C.

options.A: Proton numbers are 17 and 19, so the two particles are different elements and cannot be isotopes.
options.B: Proton numbers are 23 and 24, so the two particles are different elements and cannot be isotopes.
options.C: Both have proton number 29 with different neutron numbers 34 and 36, so they are isotopes; the electron difference only shows one is ionised.
options.D: Proton numbers are 32 and 31, so the two particles are different elements and cannot be isotopes.
